services.name: Blue Angels Practice and Dolphin Cruise
services.desc: Adults $55.00: Children 5-12: $45.00 Children 4 and under $30.00 About This is a 3 Hour Dolphin Cruise and Blue Angels Practice Tour on Pensacola Bay. Cruise is on our 42' powerboat tritoon passenger vessel, the Jolly Dolphin. We cover a 20 mile round trip, watching for dolphins, and other marine life, while passing by iconic Pensacola Beach landmarks, such as Fort Pickens, the Pensacola Naval Air Station, and the Pensacola Lighthouse. Our cruise stops at Sand Island, a 40 ft sand dune island, where you can view the Blues up close and personal. This island is across from the Pensacola Angels & Dolphins, the ultimate cruise! Up to 28 guests or 40 guests

services.name: 4-Hour Jolly Mon Sailing Adventure (up to 6 guests)
services.desc: Climb aboard the Jolly Mon, our 27' sailboat, for a 4 hour sailing adventure with optional swim or snorkel stop! This extended sailing excursion allows plenty of time to cover a lot of water, cruising around Pensacola Bay, Santa Rosa Sound, and/or the Pensacola Pass (entrance to the Gulf of Mexico). Route will depend on conditions. During this cruise we will sail along the beautiful landscape of the National Seashore, taking in the sights and sounds of the open water. Sit back and relax, or take the helm to experience the real joy of sailing! Enjoy the wind in your hair while you look out for Sail away on the Bay! Plenty of time to get a real feel for sailing, and cover lots of water!

services.name: Earlybird Private Dolphin Cruise (up to 6 passengers)
services.desc: > One of our most popular tours is the dolphin cruise. We offer 2 hour dolphin cruises by powerboat. Pensacola Bay, Santa Rosa Sound and the Gulf of Mexico are home to many pods of Bottlenose Dolphin. These wild dolphins are naturally curious and inclined to investigate boats traveling the waters of their home. Though swimming with dolphins is prohibited by law, viewing them by boat in their natural habitat is an amazing encounter. faq.a: We sail in the protected waters of Santa Rosa Sound and Pensacola Bay, where conditions are quite favorable for boating. Seasickness is highly unlikely to occur while sailing, as it is generally a much smoother ride than you get on a powerboat. The sails stabilize the boat and keep it from rolling and pitching. Also there are no noxious engine fumes to contend with, which often contributes to the problem. To date, none of our passengers have experienced seasickness on our vessels.
